title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
caption: The lensing galaxy cluster MACS J0454.1-0300, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, L. Furtak, S. Fujimoto

recognition.text: Ranked #12 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Golden galaxies crowd the middle of this Webb picture, the largest and brightest at the center, while heavily distorted orange galaxies curve around them in a great arc. The golden ones belong to the cluster MACS J0454.1-0300, seen at a time when the cosmos was around 8 billion years old. The orange ones lie much farther away.

Those distant galaxies look smeared because of gravitational lensing, in which the cluster's enormous mass bends and magnifies light from objects behind it. Even at the edges of the frame, small reddish galaxies have been bent into tiny arcs.

Lensing can also create several images of one galaxy. Four or more is rare, seen in only 10–20% of clusters, yet researchers found that arrangement twice here, the first time it has appeared more than once in the same cluster. The lensed images show a lone galaxy from only 800 million years after the Big Bang, and a merging group of galaxies from 2 billion years after it.
scale: Some bright knots in the lensed galaxies correspond to regions as small as 5 light-years across, according to ESA/Webb.

understand.summary: Webb's NIRCam observed across near-infrared wavelengths, mapped from purple and blue for the shortest filters through cyan, green, yellow and orange to red for the longest.
understand.eye: This near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and Webb's sensitivity to red light reveals hundreds of galaxies missing from an earlier Hubble view.

explore: Some bright knots in these lensed areas are magnified by a factor of more than 300. Compared with an earlier Hubble image of the same cluster, Webb reveals hundreds of galaxies that were always there but went unseen, because Webb is far more sensitive to their redder light. One program behind the data will watch a lensed galaxy here for hugely magnified single stars.
alt: A galaxy cluster of golden elliptical galaxies with the brightest at the center, surrounded by stretched orange galaxies forming an arc, plus a few bluish-white galaxies and stars.
